prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string value whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON when the annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`). Both PRs add a helper to detect this shape and skip pre-parsing. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string value whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, which corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON when the annotation is a union containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`). Both PRs add a helper to detect this shape and skip pre-parsing. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks raw type identity of each union member against a fixed set {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}. Pydantic does not unwrap Annotated when it appears nested inside a Union member (only a top-level Annotated on the field gets merged into FieldInfo), so for the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern, the union member stays `Annotated[str, FieldInfo(...)]`, which fails the `in _SIMPLE_TYPES` check and is still pre-parsed — leaving the described-optional-string case (the scenario named in the bug) unfixed. 3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and applies it to each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly classified as safe-to-skip.

prs.author: ulofiai

clusters.pick_reason: 2032's _should_pre_parse_json checks raw type identity of each union member against a fixed set {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}. Pydantic does not unwrap Annotated when it appears nested inside a Union member (only a top-level Annotated on the field gets merged into FieldInfo), so for the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern, the union member stays `Annotated[str, FieldInfo(...)]`, which fails the `in _SIMPLE_TYPES` check and is still pre-parsed — leaving the described-optional-string case (the scenario named in the bug) unfixed. 3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and applies it to each union member before checking, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly classified as safe-to-skip.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 makes a single, minimal change to the existing primitive: it dedents so `context.lock` is released before `response = yield request` and is only re-acquired separately around the 401 and 403 handling blocks, directly targeting the described SSE-stream-stall scenario without changing the lock type. #3243 addresses the same contention problem but replaces `anyio.Lock` with two `anyio.Semaphore` fields (`lock` and a new `flow_lock`) on `OAuthContext` — a larger, more invasive structural change with broader blast radius across the dataclass. #2858's visible diff only shows an unrelated `httpx2`→`httpx` import/docstring cleanup (also present verbatim in #2779), indicating it's rebased on a stale base; the actual lock-narrowing hunk isn't shown, making it harder to verify it applies cleanly against current main without conflicts.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the in-flight check on str(message.id), which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (integer 1 and string "1" hash the same) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to GET_STREAM_KEY, so it can false-positive a 409 or share the standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving _request_stream_key() ('i:'/'s:' prefixes) that keeps int/string ids distinct and provably can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, plus adds explicit StreamId/EventId aliases used consistently at the routing layer — a strict superset fix for the same bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #3262 adds __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class and restores instances via MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + __dict__, so any current or future subclass is pickle-safe with zero special-casing; its test file imports NoBackChannelError in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses. #2555 only defines __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so other subclasses with custom constructors (e.g. NoBackChannelError) remain broken - a narrower point-fix for the same root cause. #2478 also attempts a base-class-level fix but its _restore_mcp_error helper hardcodes 'if exc_type is UrlElicitationRequiredError' to call a different reconstructor, coupling the shared restore path to one specific subclass, and rebuilds instances from ErrorData via from_error_data (a lossy wire-format round-trip) rather than preserving the actual instance __dict__ as #3262 does.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 makes a single, minimal change to the existing primitive: it dedents so `context.lock` is released before `response = yield request` and is only re-acquired separately around the 401 and 403 handling blocks, directly targeting the described SSE-stream-stall scenario without changing the lock type. #3243 addresses the same contention problem but replaces `anyio.Lock` with two `anyio.Semaphore` fields (`lock` and a new `flow_lock`) on `OAuthContext` — a larger, more invasive structural change with broader blast radius across the dataclass. #2858's visible diff only shows an unrelated `httpx2`→`httpx` import/docstring cleanup (also present verbatim in #2779), indicating it's rebased on a stale base; the actual lock-narrowing hunk isn't shown, making it harder to verify it applies cleanly against current main without conflicts.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the in-flight check on str(message.id), which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids (integer 1 and string "1" hash the same) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to GET_STREAM_KEY, so it can false-positive a 409 or share the standalone GET slot. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving _request_stream_key() ('i:'/'s:' prefixes) that keeps int/string ids distinct and provably can't collide with GET_STREAM_KEY, plus adds explicit StreamId/EventId aliases used consistently at the routing layer — a strict superset fix for the same bug.
